name: Which small gaps occur between consecutive integers coprime to 29#
description: construct() -> up to 200 certificates [x, g] with 1 <= x <= 29# = 6469693230 and 2 <= g <= 1000, where x and x + g are coprime to 29# and every integer strictly between them shares a prime factor with 29#. The score is the largest L such that each even gap 2, 4, ..., L is certified. Maximize; the optimum is 46 (the gap 48 does not occur). For 29# every even gap up to 46 occurs and 48 does not, so the optimum is 46.

sources.locator: C. Hooley, On the difference of consecutive numbers prime to n (1963). Crossref record inspected (Hooley studies the distribution of differences between consecutive reduced residues). Erdős Problem #854 page inspected (Erdős first expected every even number up to the maximal gap to occur, then doubted it after computations of Lacampagne and Selfridge for 13#). OEIS A389839 inspected: the smallest even number that is not a gap between consecutive integers coprime to 29# is 48. For 29# every even gap up to 46 occurs and 48 does not, so the optimum is 46.
